title: PMS vs mutual fund vs AIF
objectives: Compare ticket size, ownership, taxation and fees.
Explain why PMS portfolios are taxed in the client's hands.
Know when a mutual fund is the better fit.
body_md:
|  | Mutual fund | PMS | AIF |
|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum ticket | As low as a few hundred rupees | ₹50 lakh | Typically ₹1 crore |
| Ownership | Units of a pooled fund | Securities in the client's own demat | Units of a pooled fund |
| Customisation | None | Some (e.g. stock exclusions) | None |
| Taxation | At fund level; investor taxed on redemption | Every trade taxed in the client's hands | Depends on category |
| Fees | Expense ratio, capped by SEBI | Fixed and/or performance fee, set by agreement | Management and carry |
| Transparency | Monthly portfolio disclosure | Full view of every holding and trade | Periodic reporting |
example: A client with ₹30 lakh asks about PMS. It needs ₹50 lakh, so he is not eligible. A diversified mutual fund portfolio is the route today.
say: PMS stocks sit in your own demat, so each trade the manager makes is taxed in your hands.
PMS fees are set in your agreement, unlike a mutual fund's capped expense ratio.
never: PMS is taxed just like a mutual fund.
AIFs and PMS are the same.

check.q: Where are the securities in a PMS held?
o: In the client's own demat account
check.why: The client owns the shares directly and can see every holding and trade.

check.q: How is tax on a PMS different from a mutual fund?
o: Each sale by the manager is a taxable event in the client's own hands
Tax is paid only at exit
check.why: PMS holds securities in the client's own demat, so every sale is taxed in the client's hands.

check.q: Which has the highest typical minimum ticket?
check.why: An AIF typically needs ₹1 crore, compared with ₹50 lakh for a PMS.
